commit.message:
add kimi-k3-day-one set: 8-task scoreboard + day-one capacity experiment

New set behind the K3 post. Two experiments:

01-eight-task-scoreboard: K3 (2.8T, largest open-weight to date) through the
same 8-task battery as Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5. Matched or beat
all three frontier models on 6 of the 7 tasks it finished; 14/21 planted bugs vs
Opus 12 (field best); the only arm with false positives (2); worst on real
unplanted bugs (1/7). n=1 per cell, three native harnesses.

02-day-one-capacity: the same implement cell returned 0 tokens on launch night
and 14/14 thirteen hours later, same model/task/prompt/harness. Root cause of
the surviving DNF documented: OpenRouter returns HTTP 200 with rate_limit_error
inside the SSE body, so a status-code-only retry forwards a disguised throttle
as success and kills the longest tool chain. kimi_proxy2.py peeks the first
chunk and retries 200-wrapped errors; absorbed 162 in one 67-min run and the
cell still timed out, so it stays DNF. Both wrong diagnoses recorded in the
write-up rather than quietly corrected.

Anonymization: ran the repo's own checked-in rules over every copied file, then
swept. Caught a gap the rules could not: the path prefix rules stop at the repo
root, so the private app's name survived downstream in run_kimi.py fixture
paths. Scrubbed it and added a wildcarded rule (Temp/<x>/buggy|baseline|seeded
-> Temp/<APP>/...) so a future copy cannot reintroduce it. The rule follows the
file's existing design: it does not spell the string it removes. Raw per-run
model reports quote the private repo and are withheld per the
frontier-vs-open-audit precedent; throttle.log is API status lines only.

five-models: Grok 4.5 reconstructed ($2.79 floor) + Grok 4.3 fully measured ($7.33)

Grok 4.5's transcripts were reconstructed on its own machine with the same
per-turn method: $2.79 battery floor / ~34K output est — the cheapest arm
(snapshot $0.31 was ~9x under). Grok 4.3's last cell was located and measured,
so its battery is $7.33 (~25x under), no scaled cells. Loop-discipline
finding added: 19 vs 68 inference requests on the same audit at identical
rates — part of the 4.3->4.5 jump is loop behavior (also effort-confounded).
"Grok terseness" observation retracted (snapshot artifact; real output is
Opus-class). Grok cost_usd cells in metrics.csv now carry the reconstructed
per-task figures; token cells stay flagged.

Add five-models-three-harnesses experiment

Five frontier coding models (Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.3,
Grok 4.5), each in its own native CLI agent, 8 agentic tasks on a real
production codebase, one round per cell at effort high, blind-graded
against planted answer keys.

Headline findings: no generalist (every model owned a different axis;
union 17/21 planted bugs vs best-single 12), zero false positives from
any arm, and a first-class token-accounting defect (the grok CLI counter
reports context fill, not cumulative bill — understating its cost ~26x).

Published: README, corrected benchmark chart, content-free scoreboard.csv
and metrics.csv (grok cells flagged context-snapshot-DEFECT), the public
audit prompt, and sanitized runner.py + grok_acp.py. Withheld: answer
keys, seeded diffs, raw reports, doc-plant/review patches, private task
prompts, rig-rebuild script. De-identified per repo anonymize rules;
grepped clean of the private app name, real paths, and usernames.

speed-depth: dated retest addenda on exp 02 + 03 finding #2

Both launch-week "finding #2" claims did not survive the n=20 retest;
add dated addenda (not silent edits), keeping the originals as the
launch-week record.

- 02 finding #2 ("parity on heavier work"): the n=1 audit pair (1.06x)
  was one lucky pair. Paired 3-file audits run 1.32x median at n=10
  [0.99-1.88], 1.29x at n=20 [0.92-1.70]. Tax flattens, doesn't vanish.
- 03 finding #2 ("~40% fewer tokens, finishes sooner"): token gap
  shrank 39%->12.9% at n=10 (8% at n=20) and Fable finished 1.49x
  behind, not ahead (43.3s vs 29.0s), reversing the launch-day lead.
  Both models now write 2-3x more tokens than these logs 48h later.

Cross-links each addendum to the fable-5-day-4 retest folder.

Add fable-5-effort-recheck: effort-dial recheck on the restored Jul-3 build

Base grid n=8/cell (3 Fable task tiers + Opus realistic control) plus a
flat n=5/cell needle tier on the proven planted cross-file bug; 210 graded
runs. Normal work: dial is a cost lever only (~2-3x time / ~4-5x tokens
low->max, quality flat). Hard work: threshold at xhigh, Fable-only (2/5
then 3/5 at max; Opus 0/25). Fable writes fewer tokens than Opus at every
level. answers/ transcripts excluded per day-4 precedent; paths anonymized.

Add managed-vs-local-agents experiment set

Managed agent runtimes vs running the same loop yourself, across Google /
Anthropic / OpenAI (all now run-by-ID over REST). 108-run clean comparison
plus per-provider deep dives, a Gemini<->Anthropic format translator, and a
one-definition-many-runtimes portability demo. Copied from the source
experiment repo, restructured to the set-folder + README-index convention and
run through the repo's anonymize rules (one Windows path -> <WORKDIR>).

Sakana AI's fugu-ultra (a "multi-agent conductor") run through the same
rigs as GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5:

- Reliability by effort: 64/64 = 100% (all tiers); GPT-5.5 16/16.
- Conductor token tax: ~1,150 visible tokens bill ~13,700 (~12x).
- Cost per run: GLM $0.10, GPT-5.5 $0.49, Opus $0.51, fugu ~$1.48.
- Planted cross-file bug, in-context n=10: GPT-5.5 5/10, fugu 4/10,
  Opus 2/10, GLM 2/10. The conductor buys no diligence edge.
